(A.4)

the system (A.3) has a solution $u\in\widetilde{L}^{\infty}([0,T);B_{2,1}^{1/2})$ with

$$
\left\| u \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} \lesssim \left\| u _ {0} \right\| _ {B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| f \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {- 3 / 2}}.
$$

Proof. We denote $X=(x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3})$ . By introducing new variables

$$
\bar {X} = \left(\bar {x} _ {1}, \bar {x} _ {2}, \bar {x} _ {3}\right) = \left(x _ {1} - t x _ {2}, x _ {2}, x _ {3}\right)
$$

and setting $\bar{u} ( t,\bar{X})=u ( t, X )$ as shown in [15], we have

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \partial_ {t} \bar {u} - \Delta_ {L} \bar {u} + \nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {u} \otimes \bar {u}) + \nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {u} \otimes \bar {v}) \\ + \nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {v} \otimes \bar {u}) + (\bar {u} _ {2}, 0, 0) + \nabla_ {L} \bar {p} = \bar {f}, \\ \nabla_ {L} \cdot \bar {u} = 0, \\ \bar {u} | _ {t = 0} = u _ {0}, \end{array} \right.
$$

(A.5)

(A.5)

where $\nabla_{L}=\left(\partial_{\bar{x}_{1}},\partial_{\bar{x}_{2}}-t \partial_{\bar{x}_{1}},\partial_{\bar{x}_{3}}\right), \Delta_{L}=\nabla_{L} \cdot \nabla_{L},\bar{u}_{\ell_{q}}^{\mathrm{non-loc}}(t,\bar{X})=u_{\ell_{q}}^{\mathrm{non-loc}}(t,X),\bar{F}_{q+1}(t,\bar{X})= F_{q+1}(t,X).$ Under $\bar{X}$ -coordinates, we define $\mathbb{P}_{H_{L}}$ the Helmholtz projector onto divergence-free vector fields by $\mathbb{P}_{H_{L}}=\mathrm{Id}-\frac{\nabla_{L}\mathrm{div}_{L}} {\Delta_{L}}.$ Then we obtain from (A.5) that

$$
\begin{array}{l} \bar {u} (t, \bar {X}) = e ^ {t \Delta_ {L}} u _ {0} + \int_ {0} ^ {t} e ^ {(t - s) \Delta_ {L}} \mathbb {P} _ {H _ {L}} \left(\nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {u} \otimes \bar {u}) + \nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {u} \otimes \bar {v})\right) \mathrm {d} s \\ + \int_ {0} ^ {t} e ^ {(t - s) \Delta_ {L}} \mathbb {P} _ {H _ {L}} \left(\nabla_ {L} \cdot (\bar {v} \otimes \bar {u}) + \left(\bar {u} _ {2}, 0, 0\right) - \bar {f}\right) \mathrm {d} s. \\ \end{array}
$$

(A.6)

Note that for $0\leq t\leq \frac{1}{4},$

(A.6)

Note that for $0\leq t\leq \frac{1}{4},$

$$
\widehat {e ^ {t \Delta_ {L}}} = e ^ {- t \left((1 + t ^ {2}) | \bar {\xi} _ {1} | ^ {2} + | \bar {\xi} _ {2} | ^ {2} + | \bar {\xi} _ {3} | ^ {2} - 2 t \bar {\xi} _ {1} \bar {\xi} _ {2}\right)} \leq e ^ {- \frac {3}{4} t \left(| \bar {\xi} _ {1} | ^ {2} + | \bar {\xi} _ {2} | ^ {2} + | \bar {\xi} _ {3} | ^ {2}\right)},
$$

by the smoothing effect of heat flow [2, Lemma 2.4], one infers that there exist constants c and C such that if $\mathrm{spt}_{\bar{\xi}}\widehat{u}\subseteq\lambda \mathcal{C}$ , where C is an annulus, then

$$
\left\| e ^ {t \Delta_ {L}} u \right\| _ {L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {p}} \leq C e ^ {- c t \lambda^ {2}} \| u \| _ {L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {p}}.
$$
Therefore, for $0 < T \leq \frac{1}{4}$ , we deduce from Lemma A.7 that

\begin{array}{l} \left\| \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} \lesssim \left\| u _ {0} \right\| _ {\mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {u} \otimes \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {u} \otimes \bar {v} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {1}{2}}} \\ + \left\| \bar {v} \otimes \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {1} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {f} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {3}{2}}} \\ \lesssim \left\| u _ {0} \right\| _ {\mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} ^ {2} + \left\| \bar {v} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty}

{t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} ^ {2} + \left\| \bar {v} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} \left\| \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {u} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {1} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \left\| \bar {f} \right\| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {t} ^ {\infty} \mathbf {B} _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {3}{2}}}, \\ \end{array}

(A.7)

here

$$
\| \bar {u} \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {r} \mathbf {B} _ {p, q} ^ {s}} \stackrel {\mathrm {d e f}}{=} \left\| \left(2 ^ {j s} \| \bar {\Delta} _ {j} \bar {u} \|_ {L ^ {r} ([ 0, T ]; L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {p})}\right) _ {j \in \mathbb {Z}} \right\| _ {\ell^ {q} (\mathbb {Z})} < \infty ,
$$

where $\bar{\Delta}_{j}$ is localization nonhomogeneous operator from the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory under $\bar{X}$ -coordinates. Then by the definition of $\bar{Y}$ , we have for $j\geq0,$

where $\bar{\Delta}_{j}$ is localization nonhomogeneous operator from the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory under $\bar{X}$ -coordinates. Then by the definition of $\bar{Y}$ , we have for $j\geq0,$

$$
\begin{array}{l} \left\| \bar {\Delta} _ {j} \bar {u} \right\| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}} = \left\| \int h _ {j} (\bar {X} - \bar {Y}) \bar {u} (t, \bar {Y}) \mathrm {d} \bar {Y} \right\| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}} \\ = \left\| \int h _ {j} \left(x _ {1} - y _ {1} - t \left(x _ {2} - y _ {2}\right), x _ {2} - y _ {2}, x _ {3} - y _ {3}\right)\right) u (t, Y) \mathrm {d} Y \Bigg \| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}} \\ = \left\| \mathcal {F} \left(\int h _ {j} \left(x _ {1} - y _ {1} - t \left(x _ {2} - y _ {2}\right), x _ {2} - y _ {2}, x _ {3} - y _ {3}\right)\right) u (t, Y) \mathrm {d} Y\right) (\xi) \Bigg \| _ {L _ {\xi} ^ {2}}. \\ \end{array}
$$

By the definition of $\bar{X}$ and $\bar{Y}$ , we have

\begin{array}{l} \mathcal {F} \left(\int h _ {j} \left(x _ {1} - y _ {1} - t \left(x _ {2} - y _ {2}\right), x _ {2} - y _ {2}, x _ {3} - y _ {3}\right)\right) u (t, Y) \mathrm {d} Y \bigg) (\xi) \\ = \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} h _ {j} \left(x _ {1} - y _ {1} - t \left(x _ {2} - y _ {2}\right), x _ {2} - y _ {2}, x _ {3} - y _ {3}\right)) u (t, Y) \mathrm {d} Y e ^ {- \mathrm {i} 2 \pi X \cdot \xi} \mathrm {d} X \\ = \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} h _ {j} (\bar {X} - \bar {Y}) u (t, \bar {y} _ {1} + t \bar {y} _ {2}, \bar {y} _ {2}, \bar {y} _ {3}) e ^ {- \mathrm {i} 2 \pi \bar {X} \cdot \left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right)} \mathrm {d} \bar {Y} \mathrm {d} \bar {X} \\ = \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} h _ {j} (\bar {X} - \bar {Y}) e ^ {- \mathrm {i} 2 \pi (\bar {X} - \bar {Y}) \cdot \left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right)} u (t, \bar {y} _ {1} + t \bar {y} _ {2}, \bar {y} _ {2},

\left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right)} u (t, \bar {y} _ {1} + t \bar {y} _ {2}, \bar {y} _ {2}, \bar {y} _ {3}) e ^ {- \mathrm {i} 2 \pi \bar {Y} \cdot \left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right)} \mathrm {d} \bar {X} \mathrm {d} \bar {Y} \\ = \varphi_ {j} \left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right) \widehat {u} (t, \xi)
. \\ \end{array}

Since spt $\varphi_{j}(\xi)\subseteq 2^{j}\mathcal{C}(0,\frac{3}{4},\frac{8}{3})$ with $\mathcal{C}(0,\frac{3}{4},\frac{8}{3})=\{\xi\in \mathbb{R}^{3}|_{\frac{3}{4}}\leq|\xi|\leq \frac{8}{3}\}$ and spt $\widehat{\varphi}_{j}(\xi)\equiv 1$ for $\xi\in 2^{j}\mathcal{C}(0,\frac{6}{7},\frac{12}{7})$ , then for $t\leq \frac{1}{4},$

$$
2 ^ {j} \mathcal {C} \left(0, \frac {9}{1 4}, \frac {9}{7}\right) \subseteq \operatorname {s p t} \varphi_ {j} \left(\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}\right) \subseteq 2 ^ {j} \mathcal {C} \left(0, \frac {9}{1 6}, \frac {7}{2}\right).
$$

Similarly, one deduces that

$$
\| \bar {\Delta} _ {- 1} \bar {u} \| _ {L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {2}} = \| \chi (\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}) \widehat {u} (t, \xi) \| _ {L _ {\xi} ^ {2}}, \quad B (0, \frac {9}{1 6}) \subseteq \mathrm {s p t} \chi (\xi_ {1}, t \xi_ {1} + \xi_ {2}, \xi_ {3}) \subseteq B (0, \frac {7}{4}).
$$

These facts imply that there exist another two dyadic partition of unity $\{\widetilde {\chi} (\xi),\widetilde {\varphi} (\xi)\}$ and $\{\widetilde {\widetilde {\chi}} (\xi),\widetilde {\widetilde {\varphi}} (\xi)\}$ such that

$$
\| \widetilde {\Delta} _ {j} u \| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}} \lesssim \| \bar {\Delta} _ {j} \bar {u} \| _ {L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {2}} \lesssim \| \widetilde {\widetilde {\Delta}} _ {j} u \| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}}, \quad \| \widetilde {\Delta} _ {- 1} u \| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}} \lesssim \| \bar {\Delta} _ {- 1} \bar {u} \| _ {L _ {\bar {X}} ^ {2}} \lesssim \| \widetilde {\widetilde {\Delta}} _ {- 1} u \| _ {L _ {X} ^ {2}}
$$

Therefore $\| \bar{u}\|_{\tilde{L}_{T}^{r}B_{p,q}^{s}}\sim\| u\|_{\tilde{L}_{T}^{r}B_{p,q}^{s}}$ . Hence we infers from (A.4) and (A.7) $_{t=T}$ that

$$
\| u \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} \lesssim \| u _ {0} \| _ {B _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {1}{2}}} + \| u \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} ^ {2} + \varepsilon \| u \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + T \| u \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} + \| f \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {3}{2}}}.
$$

Therefore, as long as $\varepsilon$ and T are small enough, u solves (A.3) on $[0,T]$ with

$$
\| u \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {\frac {1}{2}}} \lesssim \| u _ {0} \| _ {B _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {1}{2}}} + \| f \| _ {\widetilde {L} _ {T} ^ {\infty} B _ {2, 1} ^ {- \frac {3}{2}}}.
$$

Hence, we complete this proof.
